lines: כִּי אַתָּה גָּדוֹל וְאֵין לְךָ קֵץ
עֶלְיוֹן אַתָּה לְבַדְּךָ וְלְךָ יִכְרַע כֹּל

review: Stanza 1 is a two-line acclamation in the Arabic and is kept at two lines; the reader prints however many lines the stanza has, so the shape must match the corpus exactly. `hebrew-meter.mjs` will report 'irregular stanza shape 2/4/4' for this hymn — that is the printed shape, not a defect, and the per-position medians in stanzas 2–3 are what matter.
2:1 עָלִיתָ מְאֹד — Psalm 97:9 (עַל־כָּל־אֱלֹהִים מְאֹד נַעֲלֵיתָ); the whole hymn is built on that verse, so the phrase is quoted rather than paraphrased.
3:3 כָּל־מָרוֹם — 'every height', for أَعْلَى السُّدُود (the highest barriers); a literal 'dam/barrier' (סֶכֶר) would obscure the point, which is that no height stands before Him.
3:4 וְלְךָ יִכְרַע כֹּל — 'and to You all shall kneel', for لَكَ كُلُّ السُّجُود; כָּרַע (Ps 95:6) replaces the post-biblical noun for prostration and keeps the line pointed and biblical.
